title: Remove Parentheses to Make the Text Valid

concept.title: Match brackets with a stack of positions, and delete the rest
body: The text has letters and parentheses. Remove the **fewest** parentheses so that the parentheses in the rest are valid (every `(` is closed by a `)`, and no `)` stands without an open `(`). Which brackets have to go? Exactly the ones that **cannot be matched**.

Match them with a stack of the **positions** of the open brackets. On `(` push the position. On `)`: if the stack is not empty, pop it (they are a pair); if it is empty, this `)` has no partner and must be removed. After the scan, the positions still on the stack are `(` without a partner and are removed too.
This choice is also unique: in `a)b(c`, the `)` and the `(` are both unmatched, so they are the ones to remove.

statement: A text consists of lowercase letters and the parentheses `(` and `)`. Remove the smallest number of parentheses so that the parentheses of the remaining text are valid. The brackets to remove are the ones that cannot be matched: a `)` with no unclosed `(` before it, and a `(` that is never closed. Print the remaining text, or `empty` if nothing remains.

examples.note: The last ) has no partner: lee(t(c)o)de.
Only the first ) has no partner: the result is ab(c)d.

hints: Use a stack with the positions of the open brackets.
A closing bracket pops a position; if the stack is empty, mark the bracket for removal.
Brackets left on the stack at the end are unmatched: remove them as well.

explanation: Matching pairs are found with a stack of positions. Closing brackets that meet an empty stack and opening brackets left on the stack are the unmatched ones, and are removed.
